Authorities in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Odisha have issued alerts, evacuated residents, and mobilized relief teams. Rivers have overflowed, damaging property and crops, prompting coordinated disaster response efforts between state and central agencies to manage the crisis.
items.title: Heavy Rains Trigger Floods and Landslides Across Nepal and Bordering Indian States

items.summary: Kempower has signed a framework agreement to provide high-speed electric vehicle charging infrastructure to all DP World terminal operations in Canada. The first two sites are now online, following a successful trial at Global Container Terminals in Vancouver. Doug Smith, CEO of DP World in Canada, stated the agreement offers a scalable and reliable platform to support current operations and future electrification efforts.
items.title: New Kempower charging deal powers up Canadian port operations

items.summary: State-owned NTPC and EDF Power Solutions India have formed a 50:50 joint venture to develop pumped storage, hydropower, and other renewable energy projects in India and neighboring countries. The agreement was signed on September 25 in the presence of both companies' chairmen. Through this partnership, the entities aim to contribute to India's goal of 100 GW of pumped storage capacity by 2036.
items.title: NTPC and EDF Partner for Renewable Energy Projects in India

items.summary: The article recounts the life of Anaxagoras, a 5th-century BCE Athenian philosopher who faced persecution for his scientific views on the cosmos. Despite the enlightened rule of Pericles, Athenian society banned astronomy, leading to Anaxagoras's imprisonment and eventual banishment. The text illustrates how intellectuals often face danger when challenging established beliefs or state power. It draws parallels between Anaxagoras's fate and those of later thinkers like Socrates, Copernicus, and Dostoevsky, suggesting that true intellectual inquiry frequently invites conflict with authority. The piece concludes by warning against suppressing thought, citing Bob Dylan's lyrics on the risks of independent thinking.
items.title: The Perils of Intellectual Dissent in Ancient Athens

items.summary: Damodar Mauzo, an 82-year-old Konkani writer born in 1944, recounts how early childhood readings shaped his worldview. He credits children's versions of the Ramayana and Mahabharata, which he read over 50 times each, with laying the foundation for his literary sensibilities. Mauzo, who won the 57th Jnanpith Award in 2021, discusses his involvement in the 1967 anti-merger poll and the subsequent agitation for Konkani's official status and Goa's statehood. He emphasizes the importance of writers as fighters for their motherland and highlights challenges in translating Konkani literature, calling for better-trained translators to bridge linguistic gaps.
items.title: Damodar Mauzo Reflects on Language, Literature and Activism

items.summary: Rising inflation and global oil price spikes have tilted the balance toward an RBI rate hike in October. Economists expect a shallow cycle of 50-75 basis points. While retail inflation reached 4.82%, core inflation accelerated to 4.44%. Experts warn inflation could breach 6% in 3QFY27, though growth remains resilient at 7.8%.
items.title: RBI Likely to Raise Repo Rate Amid Rising Inflation Pressures

items.summary: Google removed a feature that allowed users to generate AI images within Google Earth following an outcry from experts. The tool enabled the creation of photorealistic scenes at real coordinates, leading to the rapid fabrication of imagery depicting a nuclear plant in Iran, a bomb crater near Gaza, and floods at the US Capitol. Google stated it would return with stronger guardrails, but the incident highlighted the risks of integrating generative AI into verification infrastructure. The article notes that detection tools often lag behind the spread of disinformation, allowing doubt to damage authentic evidence before facts can be verified.
items.title: Google Recalls AI Feature After Users Generate Fake War Imagery

items.summary: Anthropic has launched the Claude Marketplace, a centralized hub offering over 2,000 connectors and plugins from partners like Atlassian, Microsoft, and Salesforce. The platform allows companies to purchase AI-powered agents and access consulting services from firms such as Deloitte. By enabling open publishing via the Model Context Protocol, Anthropic aims to improve product discovery and avoid the pitfalls faced by OpenAI's previous marketplace attempt.
items.title: Anthropic Launches Marketplace for AI Tools and Plugins

items.summary: Sources close to negotiations suggest a US-India trade deal could protect India from a potential 100 per cent tariff under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. The deal might also shield India from Section 301 investigation actions regarding excess capacity. While New Delhi has negotiated the deal, it insists on securing an advantage over competing economies before finalizing it. India maintains it will not stop purchasing Russian oil due to energy security needs for its 1.4 billion population.
items.title: Sources say US-India trade deal could shield India from Russian sanctions tariffs

items.summary: Preparations are underway for the centenary of the Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama, scheduled for January 28 to 31, 2027, at Wadi Haramayn. The four-day event will focus on social empowerment, covering children, youth, and senior citizens. Plans include 630 Tasqiya conferences in Kerala, discussions at 130 centres on over 100 social issues, and support from the Sunni Students Federation's 25,000 members.
items.title: Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama prepares for 2027 centenary

items.summary: Keshi Dalai, 75, survived nearly 25 km in the Brahmani River after falling into swollen floodwaters in Odisha. Rescued on Sunday morning, she had drifted for over 12 hours in darkness. Her son-in-law reported the discovery, while rescuers noted her pale condition. Officials cite seven flood deaths, though experts allege underreporting. The region faces further flooding.
items.title: 75-Year-Old Woman Survives 25 Km Drift in Odisha Floods

items.summary: Following the 2024 NEET paper leak and subsequent Supreme Court reprimand, the National Testing Agency has deployed 39 CISF personnel to guard its confidential examination areas in New Delhi. The agency has shifted sensitive operations to a new 55,000 square feet facility on Minto Road, implementing strict access controls, screening, and live monitoring. These measures address gaps identified in a CBI chargesheet, which cited a lack of entry checks and live CCTV monitoring. Additionally, the NTA is strengthening cybersecurity through encryption standards, dedicated audits by CERT-In and C-DAC, and the appointment of a Chief Information Security Officer.
items.title: NTA tightens security after NEET paper leak controversy

items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government withdrew a notification exempting the Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information Act hours after issuing it. The move, which classified the department as an intelligence organization, faced criticism from political leaders including Karti Chidambaram and Tamilisai Soundararajan. The government did not provide a specific reason for the withdrawal or the initial exemption.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Govt Withdraws RTI Exemption for Law and Order Dept Amid Backlash

items.summary: The Straits Times argues that journalism's survival depends on focusing on tasks AI cannot perform, such as empathy and moral intuition, rather than competing on speed and scale. While global trust in news has fallen to 37 per cent, Singapore maintains high trust at just under 80 per cent, though this requires daily effort. The publication warns that treating news as a commodity leads to replacement by machines. To protect credibility, The Straits Times is shifting from reach to relationships, emphasizing human oversight, transparency, and community engagement. It plans to expand face-to-face dialogues and invest in narrative journalism that captures human experiences, ensuring technology remains a tool rather than a master. Publisher A.G. Sulzberger and Minister Indranee Rajah have highlighted the dangers of passivity and the irreplaceable value of human understanding in reporting.
items.title: Singapore Newsroom Prioritizes Human Judgment Over AI Scale Amid Trust Crisis

items.summary: On Sunday, November 1, 2026, Americans will gain an extra hour as daylight saving time ends. At 2 AM local daylight time, clocks will fall back to 1 AM standard time across most of the United States. This change, overseen by the US Department of Transportation, marks the return to standard time for winter months. The shift occurs immediately after Halloween, potentially offering additional sleep time for those celebrating late. While connected devices adjust automatically, traditional clocks require manual resetting. This annual transition has been established by the Uniform Time Act of 1966, with the current schedule extended in 2005.
items.title: Americans Gain Extra Hour as Daylight Saving Time Ends in 2026

items.summary: Over 7,034 candidates were absent for TNPSC Group I and IA exams held in Salem, Namakkal, Dharmapuri, and Krishnagiri districts on September 27, 2026. The Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission conducted the exams at 31 centers in Salem, 19 in Namakkal, 13 in Krishnagiri, and 25 in Dharmapuri. District Collectors inspected various exam centers across these regions.
items.title: Over 7,000 Candidates Absent for TNPSC Group I Exams in Salem Region

items.summary: A Zonal Railway Users Consultative Committee member has appealed for the immediate restoration of direct train services between Visakhapatnam and Narasapur, citing commuter hardships caused by the withdrawal of previous trains. The member highlighted that passenger footfall at Narasapur station more than doubled to over 7.48 lakh, with earnings jumping to ₹18.27 crore between FY 2021-22 and FY 2022-23. While a final decision rests with the Railway Board, the member has urged the South Coast Railway to operate direct special trains during major festive periods.
items.title: ZRUCC member seeks direct train restoration between Visakhapatnam and Narasapur

items.summary: Bank unions in India have called a three-day nationwide strike starting Monday, demanding a five-day working week and other pending issues. While branches of new generation private sector banks like ICICI, HDFC, and Axis will remain open, public sector banks and regional rural banks face disruptions to cheque clearance and cash services. Digital banking and online services are expected to remain available. The United Forum of Bank Unions, representing seven unions, previously held a one-day strike on September 11 and threatens an indefinite strike from October 26, 2026, if demands are not met. The finance ministry urged employees to resolve issues through dialogue, noting that some demands, such as the withdrawal of the performance-linked incentive scheme, have been put in abeyance.
items.title: Nationwide Bank Strike Disrupts Services as Unions Demand Five-Day Week

items.summary: A viral video shows vehicles queuing inside a residential society in Bengaluru's Varthur area, with some commuters taking 30 minutes to exit. While social media users joke about the situation, entrepreneur Ritish Reddy shared footage of multi-hour jams on Varthur Road. Bengaluru Traffic Police sources attribute the congestion to ongoing infrastructure work in the area.
items.title: Residents and officials cite severe traffic congestion in Bengaluru's Varthur area

items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim to have seized a second US underwater drone, identified as a REMUS 600, during a reconnaissance mission in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC Navy states the vessel was intercepted following a coordinated operation and handed over to experts for data retrieval. Neither US Central Command nor the Department of Defense has confirmed or denied the claim. Tehran also asserts the strait is closed to unauthorized passage.
items.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Claim Seizure of Second US Underwater Drone in Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: At least six students at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute in Kolkata were injured on Sunday following an attack after they objected to a campus event organized by a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh-affiliated group. The students' union stated they were not informed beforehand and claimed attackers used knives and stones. The consumer group that rented the venue disputed this account, alleging its members were attacked first. Police have since been deployed to maintain law and order.
items.title: Students Injured After Confronting RSS-Linked Event at Kolkata Film Institute

items.summary: Millennial mothers describe feeling overwhelmed by the conflicting demands of full-time careers and intensive parenting. Katherine, a mother of two, sought advice from ChatGPT to manage her schedule but received only a blunt assessment that she is not parenting as she wants. Research from The Parenthood indicates the economic cost of raising multiple children has risen significantly, with costs increasing by 134% in two decades while household income grew by only 102%. Data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics shows single mothers and mothers with partners report high levels of time stress. Professor Lyn Craig notes that despite shifts in the workplace, domestic labor divisions have not changed sufficiently, leaving women to manage increased paid work alongside care responsibilities. Many mothers express a desire to reduce working hours but fear financial instability or professional repercussions.
items.title: Millennial mothers face impossible juggle of career and parenting

items.summary: Armin Alimardani, a Western Sydney University lecturer, warns that using AI to mark assignments could threaten higher education, citing risks of 'verification drift' where overworked staff fail to catch AI errors. While some Australian universities allow staff to use AI for efficiency, others like the University of Melbourne and University of Sydney prohibit it in marking. Queensland University of Technology faces staff concerns over job security and the integrity of assessments. Students also express skepticism, with one noting they would not pay for a degree marked by AI. Universities remain divided, with some adopting cautious, human-centred approaches while others develop policies to maintain human oversight in grading.
items.title: Academics Debate AI Marking Risks and Benefits in Higher Education

items.summary: The EPA announced a rollback of power plant emission regulations, expected to add 123 million metric tonnes of CO2. The move reverses Biden-era standards, citing no material climate impact, while facing criticism from environmental groups and scientific consensus.
items.title: EPA Announces Power Plant Emission Rollback Under Trump Administration

items.summary: A report by the Association for Democratic Reforms and National Election Watch states that 111 MPs and MLAs changed parties between 2022 and 2026. Nagaland and West Bengal recorded the highest movements. The NPF and BJP received the most lawmakers, while the NDPP, AITC, and Congress saw the most exits. The report notes that comprehensive official data on such cases is not systematically maintained.
items.title: Report: 111 Indian lawmakers switched parties in four years

items.summary: Unrest erupted at Lovely Professional University in Punjab following rape rumours, leading to stone pelting and arson. The administration denied the allegations while police registered an FIR. Simultaneously, a political controversy emerged over Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with allegations from a former Kerala Chief Secretary prompting demands for his resignation from opposition parties.
items.title: Unrest at LPU and Election Commission Controversy

items.summary: The Okapi Cancer Foundation in Abuja called for increased support and early screening for childhood cancer during an awareness walk marking its 10-year anniversary. Hope Tobi, a child survivor, shared her encouragement, while founder Oluwakemi Adekanye expressed optimism that the government will prioritize the issue. The foundation noted that over 250 children have received support and emphasized the need for public education on symptoms and support.
items.title: Okapi Cancer Foundation Urges Early Screening for Childhood Cancer

items.summary: A month before Serbia's early parliamentary elections, high-ranking politicians from ruling and opposition parties engaged in a televised debate on the N1 channel, ending a prolonged boycott. The event drew significant public attention, becoming the most watched programme during its time slot with a rating of over 48 points. Ana Brnabic, Speaker of the outgoing parliament, faced Mirjana Nikolic, top candidate of the opposition Student List. The debate covered education, corruption, and societal turmoil, sparked by student protests following a canopy collapse that killed 16 people in November 2024. Both sides exchanged heated accusations, with Brnabic citing government achievements in education funding and teacher salaries, while Nikolic questioned the practical impact of these increases. The debate highlighted the polarised media landscape and the shifting dynamics in Serbian politics.
items.title: Serbian politicians debate on N1 ahead of election

items.summary: The father of a 22-year-old student found dead at a Guwahati homestay alleges she was gang-raped and murdered. He claims she called her mother around 2am reporting torture before her phone was switched off. Police arrested a suspected boyfriend and found multiple injuries but no blood. While the father demands a thorough investigation, police have not confirmed the gang rape allegation and state the cause of death is yet to be ascertained.
items.title: Father Alleges Gang Rape and Murder of Student Found Dead in Guwahati

items.summary: India secured two silver medals and three bronze medals in athletics at the Asian Games in Nagoya. Ancy Sojan and Sarvesh Kushare took silver in the women's long jump and men's high jump, respectively. Parul Chaudhary and Harita Bhadra won bronze in the 3000m steeplechase and 200m final. In squash, Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh won silvers but missed Olympic berths. Indian boxing saw three athletes reach the semifinals, while badminton ended without individual medals. India now has 37 total medals with four gold and 16 bronze.
items.title: India Wins Two Silvers and Three Bronzes at Asian Games

items.summary: Violent clashes occurred between students and Punjab Police outside Lovely Professional University in Phagwara, resulting in damaged vehicles. The unrest followed unverified online claims of a gang rape and a student's suicide. While police registered an FIR and formed an investigation team, officials denied the allegations as false and baseless, stating no evidence linked the suicide to the rape claim. Talks between police, management, and students failed to quell the protests.
items.title: Students Clash with Police Outside LPU Following Unverified Allegations

items.summary: The Maharashtra Badminton Association elected Arun Lakhani as President and Siddharth Patil as Honorary General Secretary for the 2026–2030 term. The unopposed election concluded with a single valid nomination for each post, featuring a new leadership lineup aimed at strengthening the sport's infrastructure and grassroots reach across the state.
items.title: MBA Elects Lakhani President and Patil Honorary General Secretary

items.summary: Residents of over 20 villages near the Madhya Pradesh-Rajasthan border rely on makeshift steamers because the Dhaturia Bridge reconstruction stalled after floods in 2019. Although a ceremony was held in February, construction has halted. Villagers cross the Chambal River in about 15 minutes on overloaded wooden and tin steamers, paying Rs 30 per person. Safety concerns are high, with past accidents causing deaths. Local officials previously ordered a shutdown due to negligence but enforcement remains unclear.
items.title: Residents Risk Overloaded Steamers as Bridge Construction Stalls in Madhya Pradesh

items.summary: South Africa reports the 11th woman found dead in Ekurhuleni over 10 weeks, raising alarms amid severe gender-based violence. Police say the victim was killed with stones, though cases remain unconnected. Distress calls to the Gender-Based Violence Command Centre rose 21 percent, averaging over 400 daily. Authorities prioritize identifying the latest victim while investigating a series of killings across the municipality.
items.title: South Africa: 11th Woman Found Dead in Ekurhuleni Killings

items.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot stated that France's military deployment to Saudi Arabia is strictly defensive, aimed at protecting energy infrastructure rather than participating in the conflict. President Macron announced the sending of troops and equipment to the Yanbu port. The move follows intensified Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities, which have disrupted export routes. France will assess the scale of its involvement based on Saudi requests and regional developments.
items.title: France Deploys Military Assets to Protect Saudi Energy Infrastructure Amid Houthi Attacks

items.summary: China's Yan Ziyi won the women's javelin gold at the Asian Games in Nagoya with a throw of 70.46m, shattering the previous record of 66.09m. Meanwhile, Thailand's Puripol Boonson won sprint double gold in the 100m and 200m. China topped the medal table with 119 golds, while organizers faced criticism for lacking a traditional athletes' village.
items.title: Chinese teen shatters javelin record at Asian Games

items.summary: India added seven medals on Sunday at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, with athletics contributing five podium finishes. Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 3000m steeplechase with a time of 9:08.67, setting a new national record. In squash, Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh secured historic silver medals, though they missed out on gold. The boxing campaign saw Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal, and Narender Berwal reach the semifinals, assuring three more medals. Conversely, India's badminton team suffered quarterfinal exits across all individual events, failing to win any medals in the discipline.
items.title: India Wins Seven Medals at Asian Games 2026, Athletics Leads

items.summary: Humayun Kabir, founder of AJUP, sparked controversy by praying for Suvendu Adhikari's early departure and asking Allah to book his ticket ahead of the October 6 Rejinagar bypoll. Kabir later clarified his remarks, wishing Adhikari a long life. The BJP condemned the comments, stating political differences should not extend to wishing death upon an opponent.
items.title: Humayun Kabir Prays for Suvendu Adhikari's Departure Amid Rejinagar Bypoll

items.summary: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar stated that India and Canada are preparing to elevate their relationship to a higher level following a productive discussion. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney noted good progress in trade negotiations, aiming to double bilateral trade to 70 billion Canadian dollars by 2030. Both leaders agreed to take calibrated steps to restore stability and normalize ties.
items.title: India and Canada Elevate Diplomatic Ties Amid Trade Talks

items.summary: Lime UK reported annual profits more than doubling to £4.7m in 2025, driven by a 31% rise in monthly users to nearly 700,000. While the company expanded its fleet and entered new cities, it faces mounting safety concerns regarding collisions and pavement parking. Lime recently introduced smaller bike models in response to criticism, though local authorities have seized thousands of bikes for littering.
items.title: Lime UK Profits Double Amid Rider Surge and Safety Concerns

items.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah flagged off India's first LNG-powered train from Sabarmati Railway Station in Ahmedabad on Sunday. He also inaugurated railway development projects worth ₹1,472 crore in Gujarat, including a ₹700-crore WAG-12 Maintenance Shed for locomotive engines.
items.title: Home Minister Amit Shah flags off India's first LNG-powered train in Ahmedabad

items.summary: Cloudflare fixed a vulnerability in its Containers service that allowed users with Workers Paid accounts to access residual data from other customers on the same physical host. The flaw, reported by researcher Oren Yomtov of Accomplish, stemmed from a shared storage pool that skipped zeroing reused blocks. Cloudflare mitigated the issue by September 19, 2026, and found no evidence of actual data exposure.
items.title: Cloudflare patches cross-tenant data exposure flaw in Containers service

items.summary: South African police reported two separate mass shootings near Johannesburg and Cape Town that killed at least 27 people. One attack in Wedela township on Saturday night killed 17 people and wounded 15, while a second shooting in Lwandle on Sunday killed 10 and wounded 11. Authorities are searching for suspects in both cases, with no arrests made yet.
items.title: South Africa Police Report Two Mass Shootings Killing 27

items.summary: Residents near RAF Fairford were evacuated after police discovered suspicious activity involving three vans and armed men in the village of Whelford. Following reports of the incident in the early hours of Sunday, authorities confirmed five men were taken into custody on suspicion of explosives and terror-related offences. At 6am, police banged on doors, telling residents to leave immediately due to a major incident. Approximately 85 households were relocated to a nearby leisure centre while emergency services, including the army and bomb squad, investigated the scene. The village remained cordoned off as investigations continued.
items.title: Villagers Evacuated After Suspicious Activity Near RAF Fairford

items.summary: Labor Department Inspector General Anthony D’Esposito warned that the H-1B visa program could look substantially different within a year due to an ongoing investigation into alleged abuses. He stated that federal authorities are building a case against companies using fake employers and sham jobs. This comes as the Trump administration tightens oversight, including a $100,000 fee order and restrictions on certain workers.
items.title: Labor Department IG Warns of H-1B System Changes Under Trump

items.summary: Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur expressed frustration over speculation regarding his future following comments by former Red Bull principal Christian Horner. Horner suggested Ferrari is his only potential destination without an ownership stake. Vasseur stated the constant media focus on his position is unhelpful for the team's motivation and performance.
items.title: Ferrari Boss Vasseur Frustrated by Speculation Amid Horner Links

items.summary: European cities are implementing various strategies to address severe housing crises and rising costs. Berliners voted for expropriating large real estate companies, though the non-binding referendum was not acted upon by the Senate. Vienna stabilizes its market through municipal and subsidized housing, with the city owning approximately 220,000 apartments and 200,000 subsidized dwellings. Basel leases public land to cooperatives, while Paris aims for 30% social housing by 2035 and plans to convert 61 office buildings into 8,200 homes. Prague built 660 apartments for public-sector workers, and Dublin introduced a cost rental program for households earning below €66,000, targeting 18,000 homes by the decade's end.
items.title: European Cities Adopt Affordable Housing Initiatives Amid Rising Costs

items.summary: Pope Leo urged the Catholic Church to admit its failings and heal deep wounds before meeting victims of child abuse in France. Addressing crowds in Lourdes, he called for courage to face the past without directly referencing French abuse scandals. Survivors remain skeptical of immediate change, noting slow progress. The Pope previously apologized for scandals and urged listening to survivors in Spain.
items.title: Pope Leo Urges Church to Admit Failings and Heal Deep Wounds

items.summary: Pakistan's Finance Minister discussed potential US Export-Import Bank financing for Boeing aircraft for privatised PIA, refinery upgrades, and the Reko Diq mining project, according to adviser Khurram Schehzad. Schehzad clarified that the government is assisting PIA with financing access but is not purchasing aircraft or providing sovereign guarantees or taxpayer-funded loans. US EXIM financing depends on the airline's creditworthiness rather than automatic government backing.
items.title: Pakistan Finance Minister Discusses US Exim Financing for Boeing Aircraft and Mining Projects

items.summary: Tensions have risen in Northern Ireland following a High Court approval of a Protestant march in a Catholic area, marking the first such event in nearly 30 years. Approximately 2,000 protesters blocked the route. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appealed for calm, warning against a backward step for the region.
items.title: High Court Approves Controversial Protestant March in Northern Ireland

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV urged French bishops to maintain vigilance against clerical sexual abuse during a private meeting in Lourdes on September 27, 2026. Describing the issue as a "scourge," the pontiff emphasized the need for continued efforts and support for clergy following years of allegations involving the Catholic Church in France. The address occurred during his four-day visit to the country.
items.title: Pope Leo Urges French Bishops to Maintain Vigilance Against Clerical Abuse

items.summary: Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh addressed allegations of slapping a youth during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar. He claimed AAP workers abused his family and that MLA Jarnail Singh sought a commission for a project. Singh stated the road, unfinished for 15 years, was finally built, angering AAP. He accused the party of obstruction and vowed a third-party audit if anyone hinders government work.
items.title: Delhi Minister Parvesh Verma Responds to Slapping Allegations

items.summary: German scientists are installing new storage racks at the German Climate Computing Center to back up U.S. climate simulation data. Leaders cite fears that the Trump administration might block access or manipulate data for the 2029 IPCC assessment. The German Research Foundation allocated $35 million in late 2025 to create a safe haven. This initiative responds to broader concerns about data vulnerability due to political interference, cyberattacks, and conflict, prompting a global push for resilient data storage strategies.
items.title: Germany builds ark for US climate data amid political risks

items.summary: Authorities reported that a vessel carrying fish traders capsized in Lake Kivu, eastern Congo, on Saturday night, killing at least 12 people and leaving dozens missing. Félix Habiragi stated the boat held more than 50 people when it sank near Idjwi Island. About 15 individuals were rescued. Residents expressed grief, while civil society members noted that despite rules requiring life jackets, many passengers still travel without them.
items.title: Vessel Capsizes in Lake Kivu Killing at Least 12

items.summary: South Africa is experiencing a surge in mass shootings, with 38 people killed in a week across three major cities. Police reported incidents in Cape Town, Johannesburg, and Durban, often linked to gangs and illegal gold mining. President Cyril Ramaphosa has deployed the army to address organized crime, while protests continue over gender-based violence. The country maintains one of the world's highest murder rates.
items.title: South Africa Faces Surge in Mass Shootings Amid High Crime Rates

items.summary: Bank unions in India are set to launch a three-day nationwide strike beginning September 28, 2026, to demand a five-day working week and other benefits. While public sector banks face disruptions, new private lenders and digital services will remain operational. The Finance Ministry urged employees to avoid strikes, citing addressed concerns, but unions maintain their demands remain unresolved.
items.title: Bank unions announce nationwide strike starting September 28, 2026

items.summary: An avalanche struck a base camp near Himlung Himal peak in Nepal's Manang district, leaving at least 10 Nepalese climbers missing. Local guides were at the site when the disaster occurred on Sunday morning. Heavy snowfall and poor weather have hampered rescue efforts, preventing helicopters and teams from reaching the location. This incident follows recent deaths of Nepali climbers on Broad Peak and a glacial collapse in the Himalayas.
items.title: Avalanche Hits Himalayan Base Camp Leaving Ten Climbers Missing

items.summary: Meta believes it has developed an AI device as part of a broader industry rush to create such technology. items.summary: A high court judgment permits the construction of 190 new homes on floodplains in north Somerset, even though the site failed a crucial safety test known as the sequential test. The ruling, described as of 'immense interest' to developers across England and Wales, clears the way for a controversial project in flood zone 3a. Ministers and experts are campaigning to change the law to prevent this from setting a national precedent. While Persimmon Homes argues flood risk was considered in detail, local residents and the Environment Agency express deep concern, citing increased flood risks and potential uninsurability for future homeowners.
items.title: High Court Allows Homes on Floodplains Despite Safety Test Failure

items.summary: Surfrider Beach in Malibu is suffering from severe erosion as the ocean reaches the Pacific Coast Highway at high tide. Scientists attribute this to a century of human intervention, specifically dams and seawalls that have starved the coastline of sediment. Research indicates that globally significant surf breaks are highly vulnerable to climate change and sea-level rise. While a record El Niño event is forecast, local solutions like the planned removal of Rindge Dam in 2029 offer a potential path to restore sediment flow. However, conflicting views exist regarding the impact of recent lagoon restoration projects, with some blaming the work for worsening wave conditions while others argue the wave was already changing. The situation highlights a broader conflict between coastal protection infrastructure and the natural migration of beaches.
items.title: Malibu Beach Erosion Linked to Century of Dam Sediment Trapping

items.summary: A viral video claiming a food vendor was attacked at Patna station is fake. Investigators used reverse image search to confirm the footage was scripted. The creator admitted making emotional videos about poverty, which led to account deletions.
items.title: Fact Check Reveals Viral Patna Food Vendor Attack Video Is Scripted
